affected_boundaries: canonical CLI to persisted integration lifecycle

observed_behavior: An accepted candidate fails immediately at publication because no rebase or proof has been recorded.
expected_behavior: The canonical command performs the complete reviewed integration lifecycle.
causal_mechanism: The command delegates only to the terminal publish method, while preparation and proof APIs are exercised only by direct store tests.

anti_pattern.structural_description: Expose the terminal lifecycle step as a complete operation.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: Internal component tests can pass while the actual user command omits required states.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: Canonical command acceptance exercises the real complete lifecycle.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: Reuse original claims, intents, Git replay, focused QA and publication receipts.

applicability_conditions: A public command orchestrates several durable lifecycle stages.
known_non_matches: A documented low-level command intentionally performs only one stage.
confirmation_evidence: Five canonical CLI cases fail before repair and pass afterward.
